Shri Manoj Jain, learned counsel for the appellant.

Shri Pankaj K.Sohani, learned counsel for the respondents No  WITH  MISC. APPEAL No. 1992 of 2016  SHRI SAJUBEN AND OTHERS  Versus  GANESH AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Pankaj K.Sohani, learned counsel for the appellants.
 Shri Manoj Jain, learned counsel for the respondent No.3

. 
 ORDER
The present appeals have been filed by the appellants against the award dated 3.8.2016 passed by the claims Tribunal in Claim Case No.450/2013.

The Insurance Company has preferred M.A.No.1845/2016 on the ground that this was a case of false implication of the vehicle and M.A.No.1992/2016 has been filed on the ground that compensation awarded is not just and proper.
2.

The facts of the case are that on 17.4.2012 at around 7.30 PM deceased Raju and Jagdish were walking towards Susari on Khandwa- NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17599 2 MA-1845-2016 Baroda Highway Road, when they reached near Kukshi College, respondent No.1 came driving the vehicle MP-46-G-0916 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into both the persons.
Both of them sustained injuries and Raju died during treatment.
2.1 Appellants/claimants filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act claiming compensation for the death of Raju.
The claims Tribunal after considering the evidence on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.6,22,625/- to the appellants/claimants.

sentences.text: 1 3. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the present is a case of false implication of the vehicle.
He submits that the FIR was registered on 24.4.2012 for an incident, which happened on 17.4.2012, thus he submits that the FIR was delayed by seven days.
he also submits that it is a clear case of false implication of vehicle because it has come in the evidence that the concerned vehicle was seen at some other place.
He states that on 17.4.2012 the vehicle was at Toll Tax Barrier at 8.27 PM.
Thus, he states that in fact the vehicle was not there at the time of incident at 7.30 PM at the spot of accident.
He emphasised that delay of seven days clearly indicates that the vehicle was falsely implicated so as to get the compensation.
4. In response to the submissions made by the counsel for the appellant, counsel for the respondents/claimants submitted that it is not a case of delayed FIR.
He submits that in fact the Marg report was given on 18.4.2012 at 7.40 morning itself.
By referring to para 9 of the impugned award he submits that it was duly considered by the claims Tribunal.
It is in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17599 3 MA-1845-2016 fact a case where the Police had investigated the matter and registered FIR on a subsequent date i.e. 24.4.2012.
Thus, the intimation was given immediately because the accident had occurred at around 7.30 PM on 17.4.2012 and the same was reported in the morning of 18.4.2012.
As regards income, counsel for the claimants submits that while assessing income of the deceased the claims Tribunal has not added anything for future prospects.
The amount of loss of dependency, funeral expenses, loss of estate, consortium etc. have been awarded, but nothing for future prospects have been awarded.

He submits that deceased at the time of accident was 40 years of age, thus in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 , 40% should be added to income of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Interestingly, this Court has carefully considered entire evidence, but it has not come anywhere in the entire evidence that the vehicle in question could not have been present at both the places, which becomes very significant in view of the fact that the time of presence of vehicle is different at those places.
Thus, in view of the above facts the appeal of the Insurance Company has no substance.

6. In terms of findings recorded in para 25 of the award it is seen that the claims Tribunal has not added anything in the income of the deceased in the head of future prospects, although it has subsequently been recorded that he was 40 years of age, thus in the considered view of this Court for future prospects addition of 40% in the income of the deceased should have been done.

After addition of 40% in the income of the deceased and keeping the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:17599 4 MA-1845-2016 other components of compensation as awarded by the claims Tribunal the total compensation would come to Rs.8,32,875/- and after deducting the already awarded amount of Rs.6,22,625/- the appellants/claimants are entitled for payment of Rs.2,09,650/-, which should be paid to the claimants over and above the amount already awarded by the claims Tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of its payment.

7. Resultantly, appeal filed by the Insurance Company i.e. M.A.No.1845/2016 is dismissed in view of the findings as recorded hereinabove and M.A.No.1992/2016 filed by the claimants is partly allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.
